title: Splitting from Julia Lee and playing 40 Highway
summary: Julia went solo at the Cuban Room; Lovett formed a band with Gene Carter and Clayburn Graves at the New Forty Inn.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, we've got them -- George and Julia Lee to talk about a little later. Now this brings us up into the early forties, and then when Julia died, didn't she? What happened -- did you and Julia split up in the forties?
Late forties, yeah.
Late forties. You were with her all the time until the late forties, just the two of you, at Milton's.
That's right.
Well, you were doing so well, what made you split up, you know, why did you split up with Julia?
Well, I don't know. We were off for a while and then she got a job in I think it was the Cuban Room.
And she was --
So you had to go look for a job for yourself.
Yeah, she was doing the single up there.
She was doing a single. Then what did you -- when she got that job where did you go to work? Did you form a band of your own?
Yes.
Where did you go?
Around town here, we would play on the highway and everything, you know.
Well, who was on that band?
On the highway. Let's see, I'll tell you, I can't --
Well, Charles will remember. Yes, Crook.

Gene Carter, tenor sax, and I remember two saxophone players you had. Clayburn Graves was one of them and Gene Carter. They were at different times, though. You used both of them. You was out to the New Forty Inn they called it, out on 40 Highway. You remember it?
Yes.
And--
Who did he have on piano? Was Joshua
No. It wasn't Joshua, it was --
Sleepy?
I can't -- no. Let's see, Joshua was with me on the highway there, you know.
That was Gene that was playing with you. Do you remember.
Did you have a trumpet on that band?
No, we didn't have a trumpet.
